1.consolidated_definition: Los caribes eran indios guerreros que, en época precolombiana, vinieron del continente suramericano a las Antillas, donde atacaron y, muchas veces, desplazaron a los taínos que las poblaban. Hubo dos clases de caribes: los que conquistaron las Antillas y los que en el Continente suramericano llegaron a una gran civilización. Los primeros, quienes aterrorizaron el archipiélago antillano, eran mestizos de los llamados karaives antiguos, poco evolucionados, a diferencia de los segundos, quienes crearon instituciones admirables. Los caribes debieron llegar a las Antillas en el siglo XIV y hasta mediados del siglo XV no empezarían a invadir Puerto Rico. De no haber llegado los españoles, hubieran dominado todo el archipiélago antillano, ya que ocupaban todas las pequeñas Antillas, desde Trinidad y Tobago hasta Puerto Rico. Se ha denominado a los caribes antillanos con los apelativos de caliña, callinago y caripuna. Los europeos les llamaban galibí, karibí, caraib, etc. Pericot García, La América indígena, p. 788.
1.en_consolidated_definition: The Caribs were warrior Indians who, in pre-Columbian times, came from the South American continent to the Antilles, where they attacked and often displaced the Taínos who inhabited them. There were two classes of Caribs: those who conquered the Antilles and those who arrived on the South American continent and reached a great civilization. The first, who terrorized the Antillean archipelago, were mestizos of the ancient Karaives, poorly evolved, unlike the second, who created admirable institutions. The Caribs must have arrived in the Antilles in the 14th century and it was not until mid-15th century that they began to invade Puerto Rico. If the Spanish had not arrived, they would have dominated the entire Antillean archipelago, as they occupied all the small Antilles, from Trinidad and Tobago to Puerto Rico. The Caribs of the Antilles have been referred to with the epithets caliña, callinago, and caripuna. Europeans called them galibí, karibí, caraib, etc. Pericot García, La América indígena, p. 788.

3.en_consolidated_definition: Caribbean hot pepper, exciting the palate in Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic and Venezuela.

4.consolidated_definition: Ave de hasta 41 cm de longitud, de color gris y marrón, con tonos rosáceos y verdes en la cabeza y el cuello, y azules en la parte inferior. (Columbidae, Columba caribaea).
4.en_consolidated_definition: Bird of up to 41 cm in length, with a gray and brown coloration, featuring pinkish and green tones on the head and neck, and blue hues on the underside (Columbidae, Columba caribaea).
